turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict each candidate's largest SHG tensor
component |d_ij|, then select the 5 candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20
pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set shows that SHG values near 20 pm/V occur systematically for tetrahedrally coordinated II–III2–VI4 and related I–III–VI2 sulfides that crystallize in tetragonal (chalcopyrite/stannite-derived) cells with \(a\approx5.3{-}5.7\) Å and \(c/a\approx1.85{-}2.0\). Concrete anchors are Cd2Ga4S8 (21.7), Al4Hg2S8 (21.1) and Ga4Cu2Ag2S8 (21.2).  

- c051 (Zn2Ga4S8) is isostructural with those three anchors (identical cation ordering, \(c/a=1.96\)). Zn/Cd substitution leaves SHG essentially unchanged in the Te analogues, so the predicted value remains \(\approx21\).  
- c075 (Al2Ga2Cu4S8) is the same structure type with only Al/Ga and Cu/Ag exchange; both substitutions are known to be nearly neutral, yielding \(\approx21\).  
- c052 (second Zn2Ga4S8 polymorph) and c050 (ZnGa2S4 defect-chalcopyrite) belong to the same chemical and topological family and therefore sit only a few pm/V away.  
- c093 (Al4Cu4Se8) is the direct Cu analogue of Al4Ag4Se8 (15.6); the modest increase expected from Cu versus Ag still places it among the five nearest values.  

All other candidates (Mg–Ga–Se, Li–Mg–Ga–Se, SiC, pnictides, halides, etc.) are either chemically more distant or belong to structure types whose training SHG values lie well outside the 18–22 window.  

Final: c075, c051, c052, c050, c093
